old_evidence.text: Beginning March 1, 2026, existing Radar for Fraud Teams users can change blocking preferences using risk settings
This control is only available if you choose the **Maximize protection** risk setting.

findings: Dashboard operators on a supporting plan can choose one of three risk presets or set a custom Fraudulent dispute threshold with backtesting. A nonmatching threshold puts the account in Manual mode. The modal projects fraud blocked and payments accepted from four months of data.

Enabling a risk setting disables the default high-risk score block rule and it cannot be re-enabled. Custom rules remain separate. The classic risk score remains available as a custom-rule attribute with plan eligibility.

Adaptive 3DS uses ML to authenticate medium-risk payments. Issuers may challenge and liability typically shifts on successful 3DS for fraud-related disputes. Regulatory/SCA-required 3DS can still activate when adaptive 3DS is off; the fraud-prevention control is unavailable in sandboxes.
substantive_changes: November adds Fraudulent card payments at Standard and above, using the separate card-only 0–99 fraudulent payment score to cover likely fraud even if disputes or early fraud warnings are unlikely. Custom rule access for that score is plan-qualified.

November documents a card-only dynamic threshold that temporarily blocks additional elevated and high-risk payments under detected fraud pressure, restores the default when the threat ceases, and respects a manually configured threshold when that threshold blocks more. The separately reviewed November plan matrix lists risk preferences and custom rules for Plus/Pro and dynamic thresholds for Pro (raw/stripe-radar-how-radar-works-2026-11-07.md:26-46).

Early fraud warning becomes documented for Balanced as well as Maximize protection. Non-card controls use supported payment methods wording. Custom Fraudulent dispute and score-rule instructions omit historical Fraud Teams-specific text, while plan qualification remains and no old-to-new plan equivalence is established.

November adds direct-charge configuration for connected accounts controlled solely by the platform, with connected-account only, platform only or shared management. Shared evaluates a single rule set starting with platform rules and preserves action ordering, including allow overriding block in either account direction. In the specified Lite or platform-only cases, Dashboard visibility allows outcomes view-only.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep the 2026-05-10 scope and March 1, 2026 historical migration statement for existing Radar for Fraud Teams users. Preserve classic score visibility conditions and the default block rule deprecation/disablement, without declaring the entire score or custom-rule attribute removed.

Keep both dated risk-control and payment-method scopes. Preserve the May private-preview Checkout bot score as dated evidence. November routes bot scoring to a distinct guide, whose 2026-11-07 evidence identifies Radar Pro and Checkout, Custom Checkout, Radar Sessions and Web Elements (raw/stripe-radar-bot-abuse-2026-11-07.md:11-15).

Retain the Dashboard overall level as the maximum of the fraudulent dispute, early fraud warning and classic risk scores that factored into the decision. The :risk_level: rules attribute reflects only classic risk. Keep card/ACH Direct Debit/SEPA Direct Debit scope for fraudulent dispute scoring and card-only EFW scope.
conflicts: The mapped summary and stripe-radar concept risk-settings section still say four controls and protection-only EFW. The concept platform controls omit connected-account-only mode and its merchant-of-record/control condition. Correct those routes using dated November evidence.

The mapped score table conflates the overall risk level with the :risk_level: rules attribute and labels the classic score itself deprecated. The old heading says Deprecated but its body and November distinguish the deprecated default high-risk block rule from continued score/rule-attribute use. The concept, index and company labels repeat the obsolete inventory or deprecation shorthand.

Separate the historical Checkout-only bot preview from the independently captured November bot guide. Preserve plan and method boundaries through the how-it-works and supported-methods guides, whose November text conditions custom risk settings on plan and distinguishes default controls from essential Radar protection. The broad May non-card wording is not authority for all methods or all plan entitlements.
unresolved_questions: The two risk-settings captures give no old-to-new plan mapping or universal entitlement for the custom-threshold controls. The newer non-card wording changes documented scope but does not date actual rollout or prove expansion for any account.

findings: Add the full November raw and dated controls, plan conditions, classic versus dashboard-level distinction and scoped direct-charge routing, while retaining May authority.
conflicts: Correct EFW availability, 'five scores', deprecated-score shorthand and blanket 3DS liability language. Preserve routes to the separately sourced plan, methods, bot abuse, platform, risk evaluation and adaptive 3DS documentation.
source_assessments.reason: The newer functional capture adds two controls, new scoring and Connect policy, and revises the plan and eligibility wording materially.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/radar/risk-settings, source-stripe-radar-risk-settings describes a plan-qualified Dashboard operator choosing Maximize protection, Balance risk and revenue or Maximize revenue. Radar adjusts thresholds and the modal shows estimates based on four months of payments. First enabling a setting disables the default high-risk score block rule irreversibly, while custom rules remain; a nonmatching Fraudulent dispute threshold results in Manual mode and can be backtested (old raw lines 14-42 and old raw line 110, new raw lines 9-43 and new raw line 147). The November guide adds Fraudulent card payments using the broader card-only fraud score and a card-only dynamic threshold that increases blocking under pressure and resets after the threat, using a stricter manual threshold when configured (old raw lines 44-72, new raw lines 47-53 and new raw lines 77-93 and new raw lines 115-123). It also describes platform control of transactions where the platform is merchant of record and three additional rule-management choices for connected-account merchant-of-record direct charges where the account is controlled solely by the platform. Shared rules run as one set with platform rules evaluated first; rule ordering still lets an allow rule override a block from the other party. When visibility is available under the Radar Lite or platform-only conditions, it is view-only for outcomes (new raw lines 158-192). The May capture and existing summary contain the older preset and controls baseline, but the summary's four-control inventory, protection-only EFW, and deprecation shorthand do not reflect November. Both captures separate the Dashboard overall risk level from the :risk_level: rules attribute, which corresponds to classic risk (old raw lines 74-80 and old raw lines 104-119, new raw lines 97-113 and new raw lines 141-156).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/radar/risk-settings, update source-stripe-radar-risk-settings. Preserve the May 10 guidance's March 1 migration date and Radar for Fraud Teams wording as historical and November's plan support condition, without inferring plan equivalence. November omits the earlier Fraud Teams qualification in custom-threshold and score-rule instructions, but retains the named controls/effects and no override of merchant custom rules (old raw lines 27-42 and old raw lines 82-119, new raw lines 28-43 and new raw lines 125-156). November adds likely-fraud card blocking, its distinct card-only score, dynamic thresholds and direct-charge configuration, and changes EFW from protection-only to Balanced plus Maximize protection. It changes non-card wording from local payment methods to supported methods and testing environments to sandboxes for the authentication fraud-prevention control; issuer challenge, qualified liability shift and SCA-required 3DS remain (old raw lines 46-72 and new raw lines 47-95 and new raw lines 115-123 and new raw lines 158-192). The plan comparison, refunds and bot links, and updated risk-evaluation/review destinations supply navigation; table spacing and emphasis changes are presentational. The May Checkout-only private-preview bot paragraph is historical and November links the separate bot guide, so omission is no evidence of removal (old raw lines 98-110 and old raw lines 121-125, new raw lines 95-103 and new raw lines 141-156 and new raw lines 194-198). Retain both raw captures, the reciprocal stripe-radar, Stripe index and company routes, and route plan, payment method, bot/Connect and adaptive 3DS detail to the companion guides. Correct the dated risk-control and scoring inventory and platform-control wording where those routes currently repeat the older model.
